Description: Sessile after their larval stage.  Social tunicates retain separate, typical sea squirt bodies, reproduce by stolonous budding, and tend to remain connected by these stolons. They have moderate-sized to small zooids. The zooids of compound ascidians are embedded in a common, colonial tunic.
Anatomy: oral siphon - mouth, leads into pharyngeal basket studded with gill slits. A ventral ridge, the endostyle, forms a seam along the basket, while the dorsal lamina forms a seam along its dorsal margin. The endostyle secrets a mucus net, which is rolled up by the dorsal lamina and passed to the esophagus. The gill slits allow the passage of water through to the atrium exits via the atrial siphon; they are homologous to the gill slits in fishes. Simple gut includes esophagus, small stomach, and long intestine emptying into the atrium. The heart lies on the intestine.

Description: Pelagic for their lifeaspan, solitary and clonial forms. The incurrent and excurrent siphons are 180 degrees apart, thus water flow through the animal becomes a mode of gentle jet propulsion as well.
